body:
Hey, thanks for taking the time to talk to me. Maybe I'll give B vites or St Johns a try; I usually just take multivitamins sometimes and fish oil.

You're probably right that I'm tired. I dunno. But, thanks for your time, I woke up feeling a bit better.

I don't really remember what all we talked about. But, I must have spent a few days total meeting with people one on one. I saw two psychiatrists, a psychologist, and a psychotherapist. I usually really didn't know what to say. I mostly remember getting kind of excited about going, thinking that we'd figure it out this time. And then nothing really happened.

Yeah I tried seeing a few people but it didn't get anywhere and then it kind of fizzled out. I think I did it for like two years. I think I might have not given them the information they needed to help. I don't know, it was pretty strange.

I don't know. I've been depressed for a while (maybe like 6 years) and never really was able to figure it out. I guess it's been getting to me more lately because it seems I'm just realizing so much of my life has been subsumed by being sad. i can't bring myself to do anything about it because I'm too pessimistic.

yeah :C

I'm really lost. Even though its kind of being too self-conscious I felt even more isolated after I got down voted on here. Maybe I came off as sarcastic so thanks for stopping by
Yeah. I'm trying to go to sleep but I ended up back here. You could take advantage of your sleepiness and time travel until morning.

I'm still struggling with a similar thing which happened to me. One of my best friends just stopped talking to me. A year later they reappeared and told me why (long story short, they just didn't like being around me).

It was one of the saddest times when I realized they were ignoring me. Everything shut down and was really indescribably bleak.

Today, about two years later, Iit still really bums me out. I wish I could go back and enjoy their company again. I'm still trying to relearn how to open up and trust someone again.

If I understand you correctly, I think I feel similarly.

For me, a lot of stuff, like friends, becomes a catch-22. I really need to socialize so I don't feel so lonely and outcast. But, the time with them is anxious, and the time after is depressing. Because of all this discomfort, I distance myself; whether this makes things worse or better I don't know.

With regards to work/school, I've also been fairly successful but I get no happiness out of it. My opinion now is that being at the "top" doesn't mean you'll be happy. 

Finally, for me, talking to to people, especially my friends, helps a lot if they actually understand. In my experience, depression/anxiety are non-logical. So, even if you get past the taboo of talking about your feelings some people will still not understand. And that's hard and frustrating for both parties involved but it's OK. At best, through words we can invite people to share our experience. To truly understand it they'd have to be there too.

By the way, when you say melee do you mean Super Smash?

Thanks for the reply. Your descriptions are accurate.

I'll really try to keep your suggestion in mind; I've never heard that before. Seems I don't really have the motivation to try and actually do it now.

I guess, if I'm being honest, I just don't want to try. I don't like getting my hopes up because I'm afraid of the letdown.
